examples.ko: 사장님이 몸소 현장에 나와 손님들께 인사했어요.
examples.en: The president came to the site in person and greeted the guests.
Our teacher set an example by doing it himself.

examples.ko: 할머니는 몸소 농사를 지어서 우리를 키우셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother raised us by farming with her own hands.

examples.ko: 부모님이 몸소 실천하는 모습을 보며 자랐어요.
examples.en: I grew up watching my parents practice what they preached.

examples.ko: 시장님이 몸소 쓰레기를 줍는 모습이 사진에 찍혔어요.
examples.en: A photo caught the mayor personally picking up trash.

examples.ko: 몸소 체험해 보니까 이 일이 얼마나 힘든지 알겠어요.
examples.en: Having experienced it firsthand, I now see how hard this job is.

explain: '직접'과 비슷하지만 윗사람이나 존경하는 사람이 스스로 나서서 할 때 주로 써서 격식 있는 느낌이에요. 내가 한 일에는 보통 '직접'이 자연스러워요. '몸소 체험하다', '몸소 보여 주다'처럼 글이나 연설에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 여행하면서 그 나라 문화를 몸소 체험했어요.
phrases.en: While traveling, I experienced that country's culture firsthand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 겪어서 알게 되었다는 뜻으로 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation meaning to learn by experiencing it yourself.

phrases.en: Our CEO personally practices saving money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말로만 하지 않고 스스로 행동으로 옮길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone acts on it themselves rather than just talking.

phrases.en: I'll go and check in person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몸소'보다 일상적이고 누구에게나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 몸소 and usable for anyone.

explain_en: It is similar to '직접' (in person), but it is mainly used when a superior or respected person steps up and does something, so it sounds formal. For things you did yourself, '직접' is usually more natural. It often appears in writing and speeches, as in '몸소 체험하다' and '몸소 보여 주다'.

t90.ax: Our teacher set an example by doing it himself.

en: to get on the wrong side of someone; to be picked on

examples.en: If you get on your boss's bad side, work life becomes hard.

examples.ko: 저는 선생님께 밉보인 것 같아서 불안해요.
examples.en: I feel anxious because I think I've gotten on the teacher's bad side.
I slipped up in what I said for no reason and got on my friends' bad side.

examples.ko: 그 사람에게 밉보여서 좋을 게 없어요.
examples.en: There's nothing good about getting on that person's bad side.

examples.ko: 밉보이지 않으려고 항상 인사를 열심히 해요.
examples.en: I always greet people politely so as not to be disliked.
I was careful because I didn't want to look bad to the adults.

explain: 윗사람이나 힘 있는 사람에게 나쁜 인상을 주어 미움받는 것을 말해요. 보통 '누구에게/한테 밉보이다'로 써요. 반대로 좋은 인상을 주는 것은 '눈에 들다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 사장님 눈 밖에 나면 일하기 힘들어요.
phrases.en: If you fall out of the boss's favor, work gets hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 신뢰를 잃고 미움받는다는 뜻의 관용 표현이에요. 반대말은 '눈에 들다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This idiom means losing a superior's trust and being disliked. Its opposite is 눈에 들다.

phrases.en: I was careful from the start not to get on the seniors' bad side.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않게'와 함께 써서 조심한다는 뜻을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with -지 않게, it can express being careful to avoid this.
phrases.en_equiv: to avoid getting on someone's bad side

phrases.en: I'm worried about getting on my boss's bad side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 인상을 줄까 봐 불안한 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to express anxiety about making a bad impression.

explain_en: It means leaving a bad impression on a superior or someone with influence and being disliked by them. It is usually used as '누구에게/한테 밉보이다'. The opposite, making a good impression, can be expressed as '눈에 들다'.

examples.ko: 우리 바깥양반은 오늘 회사에서 늦게 와요.
examples.en: My husband will come home late from work today.
Is your husband doing well these days?
If your husband is home, please come together.
My husband likes kimchi stew the best.

examples.ko: 옆집 아주머니가 바깥양반 자랑을 한참 했어요.
examples.en: The lady next door bragged about her husband for a long time.
I'll ask my husband and get back to you.

explain: 나이 드신 분들이 자기 남편을 남에게 말하거나, 남의 남편을 높여 부를 때 써요. 젊은 사람들은 보통 '남편'이라고 해요. 짝이 되는 말은 '안사람'이에요.

phrases.en: My husband cooks very well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바깥양반'과 같은 뜻이지만 나이와 상관없이 누구나 쓰는 가장 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, but it is the standard word anyone of any age can use.

phrases.en: My husband really loves fishing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 드신 분이 자기 남편을 남에게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An older person's way of referring to their own husband when speaking to others.

phrases.en: Ma'am, when is your husband coming?
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 남편을 높여서 말할 때 '께서'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '께서' honors someone else's husband when speaking about him.

explain_en: Older speakers use it for their own husband when talking to others, or to refer politely to someone else's husband. Younger people usually just say '남편'. Its counterpart is '안사람' (wife).

t90.ax: Is your husband doing well these days?

examples.ko: 어른께 물건을 드릴 때 두 손으로 드리는 것도 예의범절 중 하나예요.
examples.en: Handing something to an elder with both hands is also part of good manners.

examples.ko: 예의범절은 나라마다 달라서 여행 전에 알아 두면 좋아요.
examples.en: Etiquette differs from country to country, so it's good to learn it before traveling.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 예의범절이 몸에 배어 있어요.
examples.en: That child has good manners ingrained.

examples.ko: 할머니 댁은 범절이 엄격해서 항상 긴장돼요.
examples.en: Grandma's house is strict about manners, so I'm always on edge.

examples.ko: 식사 범절을 배우려고 책을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a book to learn table manners.

examples.ko: 집안 범절을 지키라고 아버지가 자주 말씀하세요.
examples.en: My father often tells me to follow the family's rules of conduct.

explain: 대부분 '예의범절'로 붙여 써요. '범절'만 따로 말하면 집안 어른이 말하는 듯한 옛 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '예절'이나 '매너'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: My grandmother considers good manners important.
phrases.nuance_ko: '범절'은 거의 이 모양으로 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: 범절 is almost always used in this form.

phrases.en: You should follow good manners at a restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙처럼 따라야 하는 예절을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for manners one should follow like a rule.

phrases.en: That child was praised for having good manners.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 태도를 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to praise a person's behavior.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the compound '예의범절'. On its own, '범절' sounds a bit old-fashioned, like something an elder in the family would say. In daily conversation '예절' or '매너' is more common.

t90.ax: That child has good manners ingrained.

examples.ko: 제 별칭은 친구들이 지어 준 거예요.
examples.en: My nickname is one my friends came up with.
I want to change the alias I use in games.
This city has the nickname 'the city of water'.
Calling someone by a nickname feels friendlier.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 별칭 덕분에 팬이 많아졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to his nickname, that player gained many fans.
Please tell me your alias as well as your real name.

explain: 사람에게는 '별명'이 더 일상적이고, 별칭은 도시, 물건, 직책처럼 정식 이름 말고 따로 부르는 이름에 넓게 써요. 인터넷이나 게임의 닉네임을 말할 때도 쓰고, 글이나 안내문에서 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: My friends call me by the nickname 'Bear'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식 이름 대신 다른 이름으로 부른다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means calling someone by another name instead of the official one.

phrases.en: When I was little, my nickname was 'Kid'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게는 별칭보다 별명을 더 일상적으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For people, 별명 is more everyday than 별칭.

phrases.en: I chose my alias before starting the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 게임이나 인터넷에서 쓸 이름을 고를 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for choosing a name to use in games or online.

explain_en: For people, '별명' is more everyday, while '별칭' is used widely for any name other than the official one, such as for cities, objects or titles. It can also refer to online or game nicknames and fits well in writing and notices.

t90.ax: I want to change the alias I use in games.

examples.en: The vice chairman attended the meeting.
He became vice chairman last year.
The chairman and vice chairman greeted us together.
I am the vice president of my club.
The vice chairman's speech was long.
Who is the vice president of our group?

explain: '회장' 바로 아래 자리예요. '부-'는 '부사장', '부반장'처럼 아래 직위에 붙어요. 높여서 부를 때는 '부회장님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The vice chairman himself spoke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람을 높일 때 '께서'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 께서 to show respect to the person.

phrases.en: He was chosen as vice chairman.
phrases.nuance_ko: 투표나 선택으로 그 자리에 오를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gets the post by vote or selection.

phrases.en: The vice chairman position is still empty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직위를 '자리'로 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to refer to the position itself.

explain_en: Deputy to a company or association chairman (회장) It is the position right below the '회장' (chairman). The prefix '부-' goes onto other titles too, like '부사장' (vice president) and '부반장' (deputy class leader). To address the person politely, say '부회장님'.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 손님이 아니라 상전처럼 행동해요.
examples.en: He acts like a lord rather than a customer.

examples.ko: 사장님이 상전 노릇을 해서 직원들이 힘들어해요.
examples.en: The boss lords it over everyone, so the staff have a hard time.

examples.ko: 저를 상전 모시듯 대하지 않으셔도 돼요.
examples.en: You don't have to treat me like royalty.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 하인이 상전을 모시는 일이 흔했어요.
examples.en: In the old days, it was common for servants to wait on their masters.

examples.ko: 고객이 상전이라는 말에 부담을 느끼는 직원도 많아요.
examples.en: Many employees feel pressured by the saying that the customer is king.

examples.ko: 상전의 눈치를 보느라 하고 싶은 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was watching my superior's mood and couldn't say what I wanted.

explain: 원래는 옛날에 하인이 주인을 부르던 말이에요. 요즘은 윗자리에서 대접받으려는 사람을 비꼬듯이 말할 때 많이 써요. '상전 노릇을 하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.example: 그는 아기 고양이를 상전 모시듯 키워요.
phrases.en: He raises his kitten like it's royalty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 지나칠 만큼 극진하게 떠받들고 챙길 때 써요. 조금 과장하거나 놀리는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is waited on with excessive devotion. It has a slightly exaggerated or teasing tone.
phrases.en_equiv: wait on someone hand and foot

explain_en: Someone treated like a lord; used for bossy or pampered people. Originally it was what servants called their master in the old days. Today it is often used sarcastically for someone who expects to be treated like a boss, as in '상전 노릇을 하다'.

t90.ax: You don't have to treat me like royalty.

examples.en: The most common surname in Korea is Kim.
Having the same surname doesn't mean you are family.

examples.ko: 할머니가 우리 집안의 성씨 이야기를 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother told us the story of our family surname.

examples.ko: 결혼해도 한국 여성은 성씨를 바꾸지 않아요.
examples.en: Korean women do not change their surname after marriage.

examples.ko: 외국 이름은 성씨와 이름의 순서가 달라요.
examples.en: Foreign names have a different order of surname and given name.
I was once teased because of my surname.

explain: '성'은 김, 이, 박처럼 이름의 앞부분을 가리키고, '성씨'는 그 성을 높여서 또는 집안을 말할 때 써요. 예를 들어 '성씨가 어떻게 되세요?'는 '성함'보다 성만 정중하게 묻는 말이에요. 한국은 성이 앞, 이름이 뒤에 와요.

phrases.en: Excuse me, what is your family name?
phrases.nuance_ko: 성만 정중하게 물어볼 때 쓰는 질문이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite question to ask only for someone's family name.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 희귀한 성씨를 가지고 있어요.
phrases.en: My friend has a rare family name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔하지 않은 성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a family name that is not common.

phrases.en: In Korea, people usually take their father's family name.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자녀가 어느 성을 쓰는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say which family name a child takes.

explain_en: Family name, written style for forms. 성 is the family-name part such as 김, 이 or 박, and 성씨 is a more polite way to refer to it, or to a lineage. For example, 성씨가 어떻게 되세요? politely asks for just the surname. In Korea the family name comes first and the given name after.

t90.ax: The most common surname in Korea is Kim.

examples.ko: 설날에 시아주버니 댁에 먼저 인사를 드리러 갔어요.
examples.en: On New Year's Day, we first went to greet my husband's older brother's family.
My husband's older brother gave the kids some pocket money.
I get along well with my husband's older brother.
I called my husband's older brother to ask how he was doing.
My husband's older brother and his wife are coming this weekend.
It was my husband's older brother's birthday, so the whole family gathered.

explain: 결혼한 여자가 남편의 형을 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '아주버님'이라고 해요. 남편의 남동생은 '시동생'이라고 해서 따로 불러요.

phrases.en: Everyone gathers at my husband's elder brother's house during the holidays.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남편의 형이 사는 집을 높여 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to respectfully refer to the home of one's husband's elder brother.

phrases.en: I gave a gift to my husband's elder brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '께'를 붙여 높임으로 쓰는 꼴이에요. 받는 사람이 시아주버니일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the honorific particle 께 for when the recipient is the husband's elder brother.

phrases.en: Brother-in-law, have you eaten?
phrases.nuance_ko: 남편의 형을 직접 부를 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The term used when addressing one's husband's elder brother directly.

explain_en: A married woman uses this to refer to her husband's older brother. When addressing him directly, people usually say '아주버님'. Her husband's younger brother is called '시동생', a separate word.

examples.ko: 신참이라서 모르는 게 많으니 많이 가르쳐 주세요.
examples.en: I'm new and don't know much, so please teach me a lot.

examples.ko: 회사에서 신참은 보통 막내 일부터 맡아요.
examples.en: At a company, newcomers usually start with the junior-most tasks.

examples.ko: 신참 직원이 들어와서 팀 분위기가 밝아졌어요.
examples.en: A new employee joined and the team mood brightened.

examples.ko: 선배들이 신참에게 일을 차근차근 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The seniors explained the work to the newcomer step by step.

examples.ko: 저도 처음엔 신참이었지만 지금은 일이 익숙해요.
examples.en: I was a newbie at first too, but now I'm used to the work.

examples.ko: 신참 때는 실수해도 괜찮다고 선배가 말해 줬어요.
examples.en: My senior told me it's okay to make mistakes while you're new.

explain: 반대말은 '고참'이에요. 직장, 군대, 동호회에서 선배·고참과 대비해 '들어온 지 얼마 안 된 사람'을 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: I'm new, so there's a lot I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 처지를 설명하거나 양해를 구할 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain your position or to ask for understanding.

phrases.en: The senior colleague kindly taught the newcomer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 들어온 사람에게 일을 알려 주는 상황에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when showing a newcomer the ropes.

phrases.en: I often made mistakes when I was new.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금은 익숙해진 사람이 처음 들어온 때를 돌아볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone who is now experienced looks back on their early days.

explain_en: New member in a workplace or group, implies junior rank. Its opposite is '고참' (old hand). It is used at work, in the military or in clubs to mean someone who joined recently, in contrast to seniors.

t90.ax: A new employee joined and the team mood brightened.

en: to be improper; to be discourteous

examples.en: Would it be rude to call this late?
Wouldn't it be impolite to take photos here?
Speaking casually to an elder is rude.

examples.ko: 제가 한 말이 실례된 것 같아서 죄송해요.
examples.en: I am sorry; what I said seems to have been rude.

examples.ko: 식사 중에 전화를 받는 건 실례되는 행동이에요.
examples.en: Answering the phone during a meal is rude behavior.
If it was rude to the guest, I apologize.

explain: 실례되다는 상대에게 예의가 없게 느껴지는 일에 써요. '실례가 되다'로 풀어서 말할 수도 있어요. 내가 한 행동을 사과할 때는 '실례했어요'를 써요.

phrases.en: Would it be rude to call at a late hour?
phrases.nuance_ko: '실례되다'를 풀어서 말한 것으로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spelled-out form of '실례되다', with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Asking someone's age is a rude thing to say.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여서 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는' lets it describe the noun that follows.

phrases.en: It isn't rude to greet first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 괜찮다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say something is fine.

explain_en: 실례되다 is for things that would feel impolite to the other person; you can also say it in two words, '실례가 되다'. When apologizing for something you did, use '실례했어요'.

t90.ax: Would it be rude to call this late?

examples.ko: 저는 이번 여름에 병원에서 실습생으로 일해요.
examples.en: This summer I'm working as a trainee at a hospital.
It's my first time as a trainee, so everything feels unfamiliar.
I explained the tasks to the trainee step by step.
Three trainees joined the company.
I walk around with a trainee name tag around my neck.

examples.ko: 실습생은 한 달 동안 현장을 배워요.
examples.en: Trainees learn about the workplace for one month.

explain: 학교 과정의 하나로 현장에서 배우러 온 학생이라는 느낌이 강해요. 회사에서 일하는 '인턴'과 비슷하지만, '실습생'은 학교 수업과 연결된 경우가 많아요. 병원, 학교, 공장에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: From next month I will be a trainee at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현장 실습을 시작하는 상황을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when starting on-site training.

phrases.en: The company is recruiting summer trainees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공고나 안내문에서 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in announcements and notices.

phrases.en: I work at a company as an intern.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하게 쓰지만 '인턴'은 학교 수업과 상관없이 회사에서 일을 경험할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but '인턴' is also used for work experience unrelated to school courses.

explain_en: It strongly suggests a student who comes to learn on site as part of a school program. It is close to '인턴', but '실습생' is more often tied to schoolwork. It is common at hospitals, schools and factories.

en: to flatter; to butter up; to curry favor

examples.en: He got promoted by sucking up to the boss.
People who flatter you for favors are hard to trust.

examples.ko: 아부할 줄 몰라서 손해를 볼 때가 있어요.
examples.en: I don't know how to butter people up, so I sometimes lose out.
I flattered the teacher to get a good grade.
Please don't flatter me and just be honest.
If you flatter people like that, they trust you less.

explain: '칭찬하다'는 진심일 수 있지만 '아부하다'는 잘 보이려고 하는 말과 행동이라 늘 부정적이에요. '아첨하다'도 비슷하고, '비위를 맞추다'는 조금 더 가벼운 표현이에요.

phrases.en: He flatters his boss.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아부'에 '떨다'를 붙여, 잘 보이려고 계속 말하고 행동하는 모습을 말해요. 부정적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 떨다 to 아부 suggests someone keeps trying to win favor. Always negative.

phrases.en: Please don't flatter me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 비위를 맞추는 말을 멈추기를 바랄 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to stop saying things just to please you.

phrases.en: He only flatters important people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같은 말이에요. 조금 더 글에서 많이 쓰고 느낌이 더 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, but a bit more bookish and stiff.

explain_en: Neutral-negative, common; flattering superiors for gain. '칭찬하다' can be sincere, but '아부하다' means words and actions meant to win favor, so it is always negative. '아첨하다' is similar, and '비위를 맞추다' is a slightly lighter expression.

t90.ax: He got promoted by sucking up to the boss.

examples.ko: 아들 결혼식 날 안사돈을 처음 만났어요.
examples.en: I met my son's mother-in-law for the first time on the wedding day.
Tomorrow I'm having a meal with my child's in-law.
My mother sent a gift directly to the other in-law, my child's mother-in-law's side.
My child's mother-in-law made a lot of kimchi for us.
I find myself careful with my words in front of my child's in-law.
My daughter's mother-in-law is my in-law.

explain: 사돈 중에서 여자 쪽, 곧 자녀 배우자의 어머니를 가리켜요. 남자 쪽은 '바깥사돈'이라고 해서 짝으로 쓰지만, 실제로는 그냥 '사돈'이라고 많이 불러요. 결혼식이나 가족 모임 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Today I'm having lunch with my child's in-law (the mother of my child's spouse).
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '과'를 붙여 함께하는 사람으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 'gwa' to name the person you're with.

phrases.en: I met my child's in-law to prepare for the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결혼이나 가족 모임에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for weddings and family gatherings.

phrases.example: 안사돈은 오셨는데 바깥사돈은 일 때문에 못 오셨어요.
phrases.en: My child's spouse's mother came, but the spouse's father couldn't come because of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안사돈'의 짝이 되는 말로, 자녀 배우자의 아버지를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart term, meaning the father of your child's spouse.

explain_en: It refers to the female side of the in-laws, that is, the mother of your child's spouse. Its counterpart is '바깥사돈' (the male in-law), but in practice people often just say '사돈'. It comes up in talk about weddings and family gatherings.
